terms.gloss: a stopping place: a bus stop
evidence: Plin. Ep. 1.13.2: plērīque in statiōnibus sedent (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 6.9.5: Athēnīs statiō mea nunc placet (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Classically a standing still, and so a place where people or things stay or wait: a post, an abode, the public places where people sat about (Plin. Ep. 1.13.2) (Lewis & Short). Its use for a bus stop is modern, and ours: no reference work has a word for one. Traupman has the word for a railway station, statiō ferriviāria (pp. 219, 397; see train station). In full, statiō autoraedārum longārum, after Traupman’s hōrārium autoraedārum longārum (bus timetable, p. 218).

phrases.latin: Ad statiōnem currāmus; autoraeda longa venit!
phrases.english: Let’s run to the bus stop; the bus is coming!

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 218, 219, 397.
